summary: 2026-07-29 14:56 PDT — The serialized rendering-context controller is generally consistent with the approved design, but outcome ordering can break dead-link detection, and a required rejection-path test is missing. The test gate could not be independently rerun because the read-only sandbox prevented Vitest from creating temporary files.

findings.title: Post outcomes are reduced in completion order, not tick order
findings.claim: Each interval tick starts an independent post and applies its result when that promise resolves. If sends settle out of order, a slow earlier success can reset the counter between three later failed ticks, preventing the AC1 rebuild; stale failures can likewise settle after Hide→Show and contaminate the freshly reset state, causing a premature rebuild in the new overlay run.
findings.suggestion: Associate each send with an overlay-run token and sequence number. Ignore results from superseded runs and serialize reducer transitions in send order, or serialize the observed sends themselves. Add tests for out-of-order completion and a pending old-run result settling after Hide→Show.

findings.title: Best-effort close rejection lacks required coverage
findings.claim: The controller suite tests only a rejecting startCtx. It has no rejecting stopCtx case for hide() or rebuild(), despite AC3 and the spec's test notes explicitly requiring proof that a rejected close still resolves to hidden intent without an unhandled rejection. The previous close-rejection recovery test was removed without equivalent controller coverage.
findings.suggestion: Add tests using a rejecting stopCtx that verify hide() resolves with isOn() false and a subsequent show() starts cleanly, and that rebuild() continues from the failed close to start and post.
